title: Plotly Code Pattern Reference
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Data Science
description: A clickable Plotly Express reference card covering chart functions, essential parameters, layout settings, saving options, and templates, with a quiz mode for recall practice.

learningObjectives: Students will be able to recall the common Plotly Express chart functions, their essential parameters, the main layout settings, and the ways to save a figure.
prerequisites: Calling a function with keyword arguments

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Reference card with click-to-reveal detail and self-quizzing for retrieval practice
keyQuestions: Which px function would you use for each of the six basic plot types?
What is the difference between a parameter of a px function and a setting in fig.update_layout()?
When would you save a figure with write_html() and when with write_image()?
commonMisconceptions: px.bar() draws one bar per row (rows that share an x value are stacked into one bar).
px.pie() takes x and y (it takes names and values).
write_image() works with nothing else installed (static export needs the kaleido package).
A template only changes the background color (it also sets grid lines, fonts, and the color sequence).
assessmentOpportunities: Without the card, students match eight px functions to chart types, name the parameter for each of five tasks (color by a column, extra tooltip columns, small multiples, rename an axis, animate), and write the line that saves a figure as an HTML file.
